listing_note: Euronext Amsterdam ordinary listing; the model is per ORDINARY SHARE in EUR. The US OTC ADR (ADYEY) is 1 ADR = 1/100 ordinary share: IV per ADR in USD = IV per ordinary share in EUR x EURUSD / 100. The FX rate is deliberately not quoted here because price refreshes do not move it.

historical_growth.owner_fcf_series_note: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - finance income on own cash, applied across the history: FY2020 334.9 (346.3 - 1.3 - 10.1), FY2022 567.3 (607.1 - 29.3 - 10.5), FY2025 770.3 (1,081.3 - 267.6 - 43.5), TTM to Jun-2026 834.2 (1,160.2 - 272.1 - 53.9).
historical_growth.ttm_net_revenue_note: FY2025 2,364.2 + 9M-2026 2,041.0 - 9M-2025 1,691.9; the Q3 update is revenue-only, so every other TTM figure runs to 30-Jun-2026.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (net revenue, FY2022-FY2025) as the historical anchor; FY2026 base growth is set at 21.3% reported from the 9M print (+20.6%) and a Q4 at roughly Q3's pace with FX now a small tailwind -- inside the maintained 21-23% CC guide.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Shareholders' equity CAGR (29.9% 3yr / 34.1% 5yr) exceeds net-revenue CAGR (21.1% / 28.1%) by more than 30%. This is the mechanical result of 100% earnings retention (zero dividends, zero buybacks), not evidence of superior returns on incremental capital; equity CAGR is rejected as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGR (10.7% 3yr / 18.1% 5yr) sits far below reported-FCF CAGR (21.2% / 25.6%). The gap is the finance-income strip, not SBC: interest on own cash rose from EUR29m (FY2022) to EUR246-350m (FY2023-25) with policy rates. SBC is small but now rising: 1.84% of net revenue in FY2025, 2.23% in H1-2026, and management says the compensation structure 'increasingly emphasizes equity-based incentives'.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 lands inside the maintained 21-23% CC guide at ~21% reported (9M +20.6%, Q4 near Q3's pace, FX a small tailwind) with the reported EBITDA margin at the newly guided 50%: H2-2026 runs ~50.7% against 55.0% a year earlier as the ~1,000-1,100 net FTE adds (incl. 399 acquired) and the Talon.One/Orb cost base land. Growth thereafter is UNCHANGED from the prior file (17% in FY2027 decaying to 7.5% by FY2035): the Q3 print was in line, organic growth is ~20% with ~2pts of acquisition contribution through H1-2027, and management's own framing is that the spending step-up protects the ~20% 'guardrail' rather than accelerates it, so the base gives the investment no growth credit and no growth penalty. The margin path is re-judged against the withdrawn >55%-by-2028 objective: FY2027 only ~50.5% as the 2026 hiring annualises (offset by non-recurring 2026 deal/integration charges rolling off), the low-50s in 2028-29, the mid-50s only around 2030-31, maturing at 56% rather than 57% -- one point lower because management has now twice shown it will spend operating leverage on growth when it sees the opportunity. CapEx 7% in FY2026 as guided, 6% in FY2027 ('towards historical levels'), 5% thereafter. Take rate at ~16.1-16.4bps for three quarters is treated as stabilised volume tiering, which is why growth is not cut.
scenario_narratives.bull: The investment step-up does what management says it will: Talon.One/Orb cross-sell (Route, Wasabi already moved payments after Orb) widens wallet share, Platforms (+44% CC, 46 customers above EUR1bn) and Unified Commerce (+27% CC) keep compounding in the 25-45% range, and Digital's volume-led +28% converts into revenue as the large-customer tiers fill. Group growth holds nearer the ~20% guardrail for longer (20.5% in FY2027, still 10.5% in FY2035, unchanged). Margin: FY2026 at the guided 50%, then the 2026 pull-forward of spend proves real -- FY2027 rebounds to 52%, the old >55% level is reached in 2029 (one year later than the withdrawn target), maturing at 59% rather than 59.6%: the bull still earns most of the operating leverage of a single-platform stack, but is no longer credited with pulling the target forward. CapEx reverts to 5.5% in FY2027 and drifts to 4.8%.
scenario_narratives.bear: '2023 vibes': the margin cut is the start of another open-ended investment cycle, not a one-year pull-forward. With no floor and no 2027 number, the H2-2026 exit run-rate (~50.7%) plus the annualised acquired cost base and continued hiring take the reported margin to ~48.5% in FY2027 and it recovers only slowly, maturing at 52% -- never regaining the 55% management called 'relatively easy'. Equity pay keeps rising (SBC 2.6-2.7% of net revenue). Simultaneously the growth side of the prior bear plays out unchanged: the June-2026 large-merchant pricing revision is the first of several, take rate slides below 16bps, net revenue decouples from volume (already 7-8pts apart) and growth collapses to 11% in FY2027 and ~5% by 2030 as Stripe, Braintree and Checkout.com press on Digital, still ~52% of revenue. CapEx stays at 5.5-6.5% because AI-era infrastructure competition raised capital intensity for good. Execution risk peaks exactly as the interim CFO hands over (1-Feb-2027), the Supervisory Board chair changes and an undisclosed executive-leadership-model change takes effect.

valuation_philosophy.headline: Owner-FCF DCF on a 10-year explicit horizon (FY2026-FY2035), three scenarios probability-weighted at 20/50/30, all discounted at a single 10.5% EUR WACC; merchant float carried in the equity bridge at the prior base value.
valuation_philosophy.summary: Adyen is valued as a single-platform payments processor whose value is a long stream of free cash flow, not a bank and not a balance-sheet compounder. The engine projects net revenue from FY2025, applies an EBITDA margin path anchored to the guided reported margin (50% for FY2026) and re-judged beyond it now that the medium-term objective is gone, subtracts D&A, taxes at a ramping cash rate, adds D&A back, subtracts capex and the working-capital use, and discounts at one rate. Three things about Adyen need special handling, each documented in inputs.notes: the balance-sheet cash is mostly merchants' money and only ~EUR4.6bn is Adyen's; the income statement carries two interest lines of which only one is operating; and the merchant float is a real economic asset valued separately from both.
principles: Owner FCF, not reported FCF: strip finance income on Adyen's own cash because that cash is separately added in the bridge -- leaving both counts the pile twice.

Charge every cost exactly once. SBC is inside IFRS EBITDA; the engine's pre-SBC margin encoding plus its SBC deduction nets to the reported margin, and the share count is held flat. Lease liabilities are deducted once in the bridge, never also from the flows.
Charge risk exactly once, in the flows. One WACC across all three scenarios; the margin-cycle, competition and governance risk live in the bear case's drivers and its weight.
Only cash that is actually Adyen's counts as net cash: ~EUR4.6bn post-acquisition own cash, not the EUR12.4bn headline.
Anchor year 1 to stated guidance, then let the drivers decay toward maturity over ten years -- long enough for the owner-FCF margin to mature before it is capitalised.
The terminal value is capped at 20x terminal FCF; Gordon binds in every scenario here (13.7x base, 14.8x bull, 12.0x bear).
what_would_change_our_mind: The February 2027 outlook: a 2027 margin colour at or above 50% with a declared floor supports the base path; anything that implies a second down year confirms the bear's 48.5% and would move weight to 25/50/25.

Take rate: a fourth consecutive quarter at or above 16bps organic would validate volume tiering and justify restoring bull weight; a slide below 15.5bps does the reverse and is still the single most important variable.
CapEx failing to come down toward 5-6% in 2027 would confirm the bear's reading that AI-era infrastructure raised capital intensity permanently.
A disclosed 2027 SBC figure: anything above ~2.5% of net revenue moves the street band and the margin path together.
Neglen's arrival as CFO (1-Feb-2027) with a clean handover and evidence of Talon.One/Orb cross-sell converting into reported growth would remove the execution overhang expressed in the bear weight.
key_risks_to_valuation: Open-ended investment cycle with no margin floor and no 2027 number until February 2027
Take-rate durability: yield per euro of volume still falling (Digital volume +28% vs revenue +14% CC)
Rising equity compensation with no buyback offset
Leadership transition: interim CFO, new chair, undisclosed executive-leadership-model change effective 31-Jan-2027
First-ever M&A integration (Talon.One, Orb) under a co-CEO who has stepped back

judgement_calls.margin_path: RE-JUDGED, NOT KEPT. The prior base path (51.7 -> 55.2 by year 3 -> 57.0) was anchored to the >55%-by-2028 objective that was withdrawn on 28-Oct-2026, so it could not stand. FY2026 is set at the guided 50% in every scenario (ten months of the year are done; H1 printed 49.2%). FY2027 is the swing year: the H2-2026 exit run-rate is ~50.7%, the acquired cost base and 2026 hires annualise into 2027, and management has pulled spend forward and expects some 2026 charges not to recur -- the arithmetic brackets 49-51% for base growth of 17%, and the base takes 50.5%. Beyond that the base reaches the mid-50s around 2030-31 and matures at 56% (prior 57%): the inherent operating leverage is real (62.9% in FY2021, 55.0% in H2-2025) but management has now twice chosen to spend it. Sensitivity: each point of terminal margin is worth about EUR9/share in the base case. The bull lags the old bull path by a year and gives up 0.6pt at maturity; the bear dips to 48.5% in FY2027 and matures at 52%.
judgement_calls.growth_path: YEARS 2-10 DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED in all three scenarios. Q3 was in line, the guide was maintained, organic growth is ~20% and management's own words are that the spending protects the ~20% 'guardrail' -- not that it accelerates growth. Giving the base growth credit for the investment while cutting its margin would double-reward the same decision; cutting growth as well would double-penalise it. Would move: FY2027 guide outside ~16-20% CC in February, or a take-rate break below 15.5bps.
judgement_calls.take_rate: STABILISING, NOT RECOVERING. 16.3 / ~16.1 / 16.4bps (organic ~16.1) across Q1-Q3 2026 versus 17.2 a year ago; the Q3 uptick is acquired non-volume revenue. Three quarters at or above 16bps meets the prior file's own test for the benign 'volume tiering' reading, which is why growth years 2+ are not cut and why bear weight stops at 20%. The haircut in the base path (growth decelerating faster than volume) is retained.
judgement_calls.capex: 7% in FY2026 as guided (implies ~9% of H2 net revenue after a 5% H1 -- verify at the FY print). Base reverts to 6% in FY2027 ('towards historical levels post-2026' is not 'at'), then 5%; bull 5.5% then 5%; bear 6.5% / 6.0% / 5.8% drifting to 5.5% on the reading that AI-era infrastructure competition raised capital intensity for good. Worth under EUR1/share weighted; carried for consistency with the language, not because it moves the answer.
judgement_calls.sbc: MEMO PATH RAISED (street basis only; zero effect on the house IV). FY2025 1.84%, H1-2026 2.23%, management says equity pay is 'a material contributor' with no 2027 number: base 2.3% -> 2.5% -> drifting to 2.2%; bull to 1.9%; bear 2.6-2.7%. The prior 1.85% -> 1.4% decline is no longer supportable.
judgement_calls.ma_pivot: Bull credits cross-sell through a slower growth decay (unchanged); bear carries integration risk through the margin path. Balance-sheet treatment is symmetric: net cash is the post-acquisition figure the company itself states, so the cash spent is removed in every scenario while only bull and base credit the growth it buys.
judgement_calls.governance: NO WACC PREMIUM -- charged in the flows and the weights. Interim CFO until 1-Feb-2027 (Neglen from Klarna, subject to EGM/DNB), chair change 1-Nov-2026, an undisclosed executive-leadership-model change effective 31-Jan-2027, and a co-CEO who has stepped back. Expressed through the bear path and its 20% weight, not the discount rate.
judgement_calls.base_year_convention: CHANGED, AND IT IS THE LARGEST BRIDGE TERM. The prior file compounded from the TTM to 30-Jun-2026 (2,573.6) while labelling year 1 'FY2026' and anchoring its margin to FY2026 guidance, so its 'FY2026' revenue was 3,088 against an actual FY2026 outcome of ~2,870. This build compounds from FY2025 (2,364.2) so FY2026 ties to the guide and to the February print. The cost of the folder's end-of-year convention this late in the fiscal year is that FY2027-35 flows are discounted ~10 months longer than their true distance (worth roughly -8% on the flows), partly offset by H1-2026 owner FCF (~EUR410m, ~EUR13/share) sitting in both the 30-Jun-2026 own cash and the FY2026 flow. Expect the February roll (FY0 -> FY2026, Dec-2026 balance sheet) to unwind most of the -78/share mechanically, holding drivers.

Order: float simplification, base-year convention, FY2026 growth, FY2026 margin, margin path, capex, SBC, weights, price. inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 net revenue (FY0). Year 1 = FY2026. The prior file compounded from the TTM to 30-Jun-2026 (2,573.6); see judgement_calls.base_year_convention.
inputs.share_count_basis: 31.567m ordinary shares at 30-Jun-2026 (H1-2026 letter). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed inside reported IFRS EBITDA, so compounding the count as well would charge grant dilution twice. Realised drift has been ~0.65%/yr (30.5m FY2020 -> 31.567m Jun-2026) with zero buybacks; management now says pay 'increasingly emphasizes equity-based incentives', so the drift is the number to watch at the FY2026 print.
inputs.cash_note: cash = Adyen's OWN cash, post the Talon.One and Orb payments, as the H1-2026 letter states ('approximately EUR4.6 billion' net of the acquisitions); the headline balance-sheet cash of 12,392.8 is overwhelmingly merchant settlement float. Own cash before the deals = 12,392.8 - payables to merchants 8,097.4 + receivables from merchants/FI 602.8 = 4,898.2, which ties to the letter's 'EUR4.9 billion'. total_debt = IFRS-16 lease liabilities only (338.3 non-current + 71.1 current); Adyen has no financial debt. net_debt = 409.4 - 4,600.0.
inputs.balance_sheet_note: The 28-Oct-2026 Q3 Business Update is revenue-only and carries no balance sheet, so net cash and the share count stay at the 30-Jun-2026 anchor. Q3 own cash generation (order of EUR250m) is not credited; the Dec-2026 balance sheet arrives with the FY results in February 2027.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Owner FCF TTM to 30-Jun-2026 = reported FCF 1,160.2 (FY2025 1,081.3 + H1-2026 553.4 - H1-2025 474.5) - SBC 53.9 - finance income on own cash 272.1 (FY2025 267.55 + H1-2026 143.23 - H1-2025 138.7). Corrects the prior file, whose last_fcf (888.1) omitted the SBC deduction and whose sbc (72.6) summed FY2025 and H1-2026, an 18-month figure.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 30-Jun-2026 = FY2025 EUR43.457m (annual report cash-flow 'Share-based payments' incl. the cash-settled plan) + H1-2026 EUR29.108m (H1-2026 letter cash-flow 'Equity-settled share-based compensation'; Metrics.csv StockBasedComp) - H1-2025 EUR18.664m = EUR53.9m. Adyen discloses no separate equity-award withholding-tax line, so sbc_incl_equity_taxes equals the expense. sbc_pct_of_revenue 2.23% is the H1-2026 actual (29.108 / 1,302.9).
inputs.buyback_note: Zero buybacks and zero dividends -- 100% retention. The flat share count is a modelling convention the company has not funded with cash. Mitigant: SBC is ~2.2% of net revenue against 10-15% for US tech comparables, and realised dilution has run ~0.65%/yr.
inputs.interest_income_note: TWO INTEREST LINES -- do not conflate. (1) 'Net interest income' inside net revenue (H1-2026 EUR8.6m) is earned on embedded-finance products (Accounts, Capital), recurs with volume and is KEPT. (2) 'Finance income' below operating income (H1-2026 EUR143.2m; FY2025 EUR267.6m) is interest on Adyen's OWN cash and is STRIPPED, because that cash is added in the bridge as net cash.
inputs.price_note: Regular-session close two sessions after the 28-Oct-2026 Q3 update, which the shares absorbed with a double-digit one-day fall on ~5.5x average volume; not an after-hours print. 52-week range 772.4-1,530.0.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 10.5% for ALL THREE scenarios, in the flows' own currency (EUR): ~2.6% 10-year Bund risk-free rate plus an equity risk premium of ~5.5% on a beta modestly above 1.0 for a high-multiple, long-duration growth asset, with a small increment for single-country listing and payments-competition dynamics. Adyen carries no financial debt (only IFRS-16 leases), so WACC is effectively cost of equity. The SAME rate applies to bear, base and bull: risk is charged once, in the probability-weighted flows; varying WACC by scenario would charge it again. Unchanged from the prior file; the Q3 update changes Adyen's flows, not its cost of capital.
inputs.lease_treatment: A: lease liabilities (EUR409.4m at 30-Jun-2026) deducted once in the net-debt bridge; lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows and no lease_cost_pct_path is used. TotalDebt is IFRS-16 leases only.
inputs.nci_treatment: None -- Adyen has no material non-controlling interests.
inputs.notes:
MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, 10-year explicit horizon (FY2026-FY2035), scenario-weighted, built on the Drivers/engine route -- routed via dcf-methods/SKILL.md as an operating company (single-platform payments processor / fintech infrastructure); same model as the 2026-08-28 file. UPDATE for the 28-Oct-2026 Q3 2026 Business Update: FY2026 EBITDA margin guidance cut to 50%, the >55%-by-2028 objective discontinued, net revenue guide of 21-23% CC maintained, CapEx 7% maintained. A 10-year horizon is required because the year-5 owner-FCF margin is still climbing toward its mature level; a 5-year build would capitalise an immature margin.

MARGIN BASIS -- read before editing. Adyen's IFRS opex already contains share-based compensation, so the guided 50% is a REPORTED, post-SBC margin. The engine's ebitda_margin_path is defined PRE-SBC (it deducts sbc_pct_path to reach the house basis), so each scenario's ebitda_margin_path is encoded as reported_ebitda_margin_path + sbc_pct_path; the house basis then lands exactly on the reported margin, SBC is charged exactly once, and the street basis adds it back. The reported paths are carried top-level in reported_ebitda_margin_paths for the guidance-comparable number. Replicating the prior file's drivers through this encoding reproduces its base IV to the cent (1,084.83 vs 1,084.81).

NET CASH: own cash ~EUR4.6bn post-acquisition (see cash_note), not the EUR12.4bn headline, of which ~EUR8.1bn is merchants' money. Net cash = 4,600 - 409.4 leases. Anchor is the 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet; the Q3 update has none.

MERCHANT FLOAT: the capitalised value of the spread Adyen earns on merchant balances held in transit, carried in equity_bridge at the prior base value (1,910.5 = ~EUR159m/yr of float income at 12x; cross-check: EUR8.1bn of payables to merchants at ~2% short rates is ~EUR160m). It is NOT double-counting with the stripped finance income: the stripped line is interest on Adyen's OWN cash, the float is the economics of the merchants' balances, which never enter the bridge as cash. The Drivers route carries one bridge for all scenarios, so the prior per-scenario values (bear 988.0 / bull 2,761.3) and their roughly +/-EUR27/share spread are dropped; see reconciliation.

WORKING CAPITAL is a net USE: receivables from merchants/FI grow faster than trade payables as revenue compounds (H1-2026 cash flow). wc_capture_pct is -5 in the engine's sign convention (+ capture x change in revenue), i.e. 5% of each year's net-revenue increase is subtracted -- the same economics as the prior file.

RISK IS CHARGED ONCE, in the flows and the weights: one 10.5% WACC for every scenario.

BASE YEAR: FY0 = FY2025 so year 1 = FY2026 ties to guidance; the prior file compounded from the TTM to Jun-2026 and this is the largest reconciliation term (see judgement_calls.base_year_convention).

bear.ebitda_margin_note: ENGINE ENCODING: ebitda_margin_path is the engine's PRE-SBC 'adjusted EBITDA' margin (the engine deducts sbc_pct_path from it to reach the house basis). It is therefore reported_ebitda_margin_path + sbc_pct_path, year by year, so that the house basis lands exactly on the REPORTED post-SBC IFRS margin that Adyen guides (50% for FY2026). Read top-level reported_ebitda_margin_paths for the guidance-comparable number. Verified: feeding the prior post-SBC path this way reproduces the prior base IV to the cent.
bear.wc_capture_note: Negative = working capital is a net USE of cash: 5% of each year's net-revenue increase is subtracted. Same economics as the prior file's '5, subtracted'; the engine's sign convention is + capture x change in revenue, so a use is negative.

base.ebitda_margin_note: ENGINE ENCODING: ebitda_margin_path is the engine's PRE-SBC 'adjusted EBITDA' margin (the engine deducts sbc_pct_path from it to reach the house basis). It is therefore reported_ebitda_margin_path + sbc_pct_path, year by year, so that the house basis lands exactly on the REPORTED post-SBC IFRS margin that Adyen guides (50% for FY2026). Read top-level reported_ebitda_margin_paths for the guidance-comparable number. Verified: feeding the prior post-SBC path this way reproduces the prior base IV to the cent.
base.wc_capture_note: Negative = working capital is a net USE of cash: 5% of each year's net-revenue increase is subtracted. Same economics as the prior file's '5, subtracted'; the engine's sign convention is + capture x change in revenue, so a use is negative.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 20/50/30, moved from 15/50/35. The 15/50/35 of August was restored on the H1 beat and the raised guide; the Q3 update cut one of the two legs of the bull thesis -- margin pulling the 55% target forward -- by withdrawing the target outright, refusing a floor and raising equity pay, so bull drops 5pts. Bear rises 5pts for the same evidence: an open-ended, uncapped investment cycle with the 2023 precedent (margin fell to 43% and took ~2.5 years to regain 55%) is now a live path, not a tail. It does NOT go to 25%: the growth leg of the thesis was confirmed (volume +30%, Platforms +44% CC, Unified Commerce +27% CC, guide maintained), organic growth is ~20%, and the take rate has now held 16.1-16.4bps for three consecutive quarters -- the prior file's own stated test for shifting weight TOWARD the bull on the take-rate question. Weighting the bear equal to the bull would say the growth engine is as likely to break as the leverage is to return, and the Q3 evidence says the opposite. The balance sheet still carries no solvency or refinancing risk; the bear is margin and yield compression, never distress.
probability_weighted.band_position_note: The house/street spread is only ~3-5% because SBC is ~2.3% of net revenue, and the price sits below both bounds, so band_position is a degenerate negative number; the finding is the narrowness of the band itself.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
